skill.name: lifecycle-email
skill.description: Draft opt-in email sequences with a welcome, promised-resource delivery, and follow-up tied to the stated customer problem. Check drafts with a local Python validator.
skill.summary: Create and validate three-part email sequences for subscribers who already opted in.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives involving template literals, CSS, documentation, byte-order-mark handling, and legitimate local commands. The optional asset renderers contain HTML injection risks, external font requests, and destructive cleanup of a predictable directory. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious exfiltration, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Demo response and artifact text enter innerHTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Create DOM elements and assign textContent for response lines, artifact labels, and artifact lines. Add tests with HTML event-handler payloads.

remediation.issue: Renderer inputs can terminate generated style or script blocks.
remediation.suggestion: Validate accent_color against a strict color allowlist. Escape less-than characters in serialized inline data, or load data separately from executable scripts.

remediation.issue: Demo cleanup recursively removes a predictable output-derived directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique temporary directory with mkdtemp. Remove only that invocation-owned directory in a finally block, and never delete preexisting output-derived directories.

remediation.issue: Optional asset rendering contacts Google Fonts.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle fonts locally or use system fonts. Document renderer network access separately from the offline Python scorer.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted specification can terminate renderer HTML blocks
semantic_findings.description: Both renderers interpolate accent_color directly into style blocks. The demo embeds JSON.stringify(s) directly into a script block without escaping HTML delimiters. A crafted specification can terminate either block and introduce executable browser content before any innerHTML assignment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source directly inserts unvalidated strings into HTML style and script contexts. JSON serialization does not escape HTML closing tags; exploitation requires rendering an untrusted specification.

semantic_findings.title: Demo renderer deletes preexisting output-derived directories
semantic_findings.description: The demo recursively deletes outGif plus the .frames suffix before creating its frame directory. It checks neither directory ownership nor prior contents. Selecting an output path can therefore erase an unrelated existing directory, and final cleanup repeats the recursive deletion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: rmSync uses recursive and force options on a predictable path derived from the caller's output argument. No exclusive temporary-directory creation or ownership check precedes deletion.

content.user_title: Draft and Validate Opt-In Email Sequences
content.value_statement: Generic follow-up emails can overlook the resource subscribers requested and the problem they described. This skill structures a three-part sequence and checks drafts locally.
actual_capabilities: Guide drafting in three stages: welcome, promised-resource delivery, and problem-specific nurture.
Require nonempty pain, welcome, bargain, and nurture text fields.
Check that nurture includes the complete pain phrase, ignoring case.
Flag configured cold-email and generic-drip phrases, including day 1, day 3, and day 7.
Validate drafts from a UTF-8 JSON file or standard input using Python's standard library.
Print accepted sequence parts and return distinct exit codes for acceptance, refusal, and input errors.
limitations: Does not send emails, schedule campaigns, or connect to an email platform.
Uses phrase matching rather than semantic review; it cannot verify consent, resource delivery, or legal compliance.
Requires the full stated pain phrase in nurture and can reject legitimate text containing blocked phrases.
Optional asset renderers contact Google Fonts and have injection and cleanup risks; they are not required for draft validation.

use_cases.title: Follow up after a resource request
use_cases.description: Draft a welcome, deliver the requested checklist, and write follow-up copy addressing the subscriber's stated problem.

use_cases.title: Support trial onboarding
use_cases.description: Create an opt-in trial sequence focused on a specific onboarding problem, then check that all three sections are present.

use_cases.title: Review client email drafts
use_cases.description: Check client-provided drafts for missing sections, blocked phrases, and absent problem references before manual editorial review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an opt-in sequence for subscribers who requested [resource]. Their stated problem is [pain]. Include welcome, bargain, and nurture sections.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [draft] for subscribers who opted in for [resource]. Separate welcome, bargain, and nurture. Keep the full pain phrase [pain] in nurture.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a local draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [draft_path] with scripts/score.py. Explain any refusal or input error and propose corrections. Do not send emails or run asset renderers.

prompt_templates.title: Compare audience-specific sequences
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft sequences for [audiences] using their documented consent, promised resources, and exact pain phrases. Validate each and compare messaging. Flag unsupported claims for review.

output_examples.input: An opted-in trial user requested a checklist. Their problem is: the trial dies after the first login.
output: Welcome: You asked for the trial checklist. Thank you for signing up.
Bargain: Your requested trial checklist is available at [resource link].
Nurture: You said the trial dies after the first login. Which step prevents users from returning?

output_examples.input: A draft contains a day 1 tip series and does not repeat the stated problem in nurture.
output_examples.output: Validation refused the draft. Replace the generic series with problem-specific follow-up and include the complete stated pain phrase.

output_examples.input: A supplied draft contains incomplete JSON.
output_examples.output: Input validation failed with an invalid JSON error. The scorer does not print the malformed draft.

best_practices: Confirm subscriber consent and identify the exact resource promised before drafting.
Use the complete stated problem phrase in nurture, then review the copy for clarity and accuracy.
Run local validation on minimized drafts and manually review consent, links, claims, and delivery before sending.
anti_patterns: Do not use this opt-in framework for unsolicited outreach.
Do not replace problem-specific nurture with a generic calendar of tips.
Do not treat a passing score as proof of consent, legal compliance, actual resource delivery, or campaign performance.

faq.question: Does this skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It guides drafting and validates text. Sending and scheduling require your email platform.

faq.question: What does bargain mean here?
faq.answer: Bargain is the section that delivers the resource or access promised when the subscriber opted in.

faq.question: What does the scorer require?
faq.answer: It requires four nonempty text fields: pain, welcome, bargain, and nurture. Nurture must contain the full pain phrase, ignoring case.

faq.question: Why can a reasonable draft fail?
faq.answer: Configured phrase matches can reject otherwise reasonable copy. A paraphrased pain phrase also fails because matching requires the complete phrase.

faq.question: Does validation need network access or paid APIs?
faq.answer: The Python scorer uses only the standard library and makes no network requests. Optional asset rendering loads external fonts.

faq.question: Are the optional renderers safe for untrusted specifications?
faq.answer: No. They contain HTML injection risks, and the demo deletes a predictable frame directory. Avoid untrusted specifications and unnecessary renderer execution.
